dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are your works really worth a lot of money?

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: When I was still alive, certainly. And since I'm theoretically dead...

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Hmm, no, I'm not dead yet. To those below, I've become an adeptus. Paintings by such beings should be worth still more.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: It's just that so much time has passed. Books can be copied word for word, and I'm afraid the only equivalent avenue for paintings would be counterfeiting.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: So no matter their base value, my paintings may have come to be worth nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: The mountains are high and the rivers run long. May we see each other again.
